Please solve this issue: When a customer cancels mid-period we refund the unused part of the current period. Add `prorated_refund(sub, cancel_at)` to `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`: the plan price multiplied by the unused fraction of the billing period that contains `cancel_at` (unused time divided by the period length), rounded to the cent.

## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-c0193] Prorated refund detail: The prorated refund report pads values to 50 characters so the columns line up.
  (learned from task T4193 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-c0194] Prorated refund detail: Support asked for prorated refund reasons as free text of at most 200 characters.
  (learned from task T4194 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-c0155] Subscription period detail: In tests for subscription period, the fixture customer cus_test_20 already has one draft entry.
  (learned from task T4155 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-c0165] Support refund request detail: The support refund request feature flag is read from settings.FEATURES at import time.

import pytest

from ledgerly import audit

from ledgerly.invoice import invoice_total, issue_invoice

        id="inv_1",
        customer_id="cus_1",
        lines=[LineItem("Seat", 3, Decimal("19.99")), LineItem("Setup", 1, Decimal("50.00"))],
    )


def test_invoice_total():
    assert invoice_total(make_invoice()) == Decimal("109.97")


def test_issue_invoice_records_audit():
    inv = issue_invoice(make_invoice(), T0)
    assert inv.status == "issued"
    assert audit.events("invoice_issued")[0]["invoice_id"] == "inv_1"


def test_issue_empty_invoice_fails():

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from ledgerly import audit
from ledgerly.errors import BillingError
from ledgerly.invoice import invoice_total, issue_invoice
from ledgerly.models import Invoice, LineItem, Subscription
from ledgerly.payments import authorize
from ledgerly.subscriptions import current_period

T0 = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def make_invoice():
    return Invoice(
        id="inv_1",
        customer_id="cus_1",
        lines=[LineItem("Seat", 3, Decimal("19.99")), LineItem("Setup", 1, Decimal("50.00"))],
    )


def test_invoice_total():
    assert invoice_total(make_invoice()) == Decimal("109.97")


def test_issue_invoice_records_audit():
    inv = issue_invoice(make_invoice(), T0)
    assert inv.status == "issued"
    assert audit.events("invoice_issued")[0]["invoice_id"] == "inv_1"


def test_issue_empty_invoice_fails():
    with pytest.raises(BillingError):
        issue_invoice(Invoice(id="inv_2", customer_id="cus_1"), T0)


def test_authorize_payment():
    inv = issue_invoice(make_invoice(), T0)
    payment = authorize("pay_1", inv, "109.97", T0)
    assert payment.amount == Decimal("109.97")
    assert payment.status == "authorized"


def test_current_period():
    sub = Subscription("sub_1", "cus_1", Decimal("30.00"), 30, T0)
